description: Fuaran DevTools relay conformance corpus. Self-enumerated: these fixtures are NOT indexed by the corpus root manifest.json, which indexes the canonical wire-format codec families only — the merge-conformance/ precedent. relay-exchange: feed requestFile to the page peer, assert the response type is the request type + ".ok" and every declared payload field is present with the stated JSON type. relay-refusal: as above, but the response must be type "refusal" with payload.class == expectedClass. relay-event: an unsolicited event envelope a client must accept. These are SHAPE fixtures, not byte-parity fixtures — treeRevision tokens, geometry numbers, resolved binding values and message strings are environment-specific and must be compared by shape, not bytes. The profile above is the HIGHEST minor these fixtures reach, not a claim that every minor below it is covered: a minor's fixtures land when a SECOND host serves that minor's addition, and minors do not reach their second host in order (section 12.1 keeps the waiting list). The relay@1.0 fixtures stay at relay@1.0 deliberately — answering them unchanged is the only evidence in this corpus that profile selection kept every minor bump backward-compatible. See ../DEVTOOLS_RELAY.md section 12.

fixtures.description: Detection handshake against a read-only host: the five read capabilities, no apply, no subscribe. The read-only host is fully conformant (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 6.4).
Detection handshake against a host that additionally offers apply + subscribe.

Detection handshake at relay@1.3: the session profile is the highest the client accepts and the peer can serve, and read.nodeJson is advertised at it. The companion to the two relay@1.0 handshakes, which keep their 1.0 envelopes and must NOT name this capability — a capability introduced after the session profile is absent from that session by DEVTOOLS_RELAY 6.3. The pair is the backward-compatibility evidence.
Typed node snapshot: kind discriminator, bound binding slots with wire-form expressions, child ids (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.1).
Recursive structural snapshot; children mirrors childIds in order, leaves carry an empty children array (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.2).
Slot resolution, resolved status — value plus the binding identity (expression + source) the relay carries on every status (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.3).
Slot resolution, noOverride status — the slot is declared on this kind and currently holds nothing. Distinct from the SLOT_NOT_DECLARED refusal (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.3).
Live geometry of the node rendered element: viewport-relative box plus overflow and hidden flags (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.4).
Ids of every node whose kind discriminator matches, in depth-first tree order (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.5).
An unmatched kind yields an empty array, never a refusal — "which nodes have this kind" has the honest answer "none" (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.5).

A node's own canonical wire JSON, embedded as an object (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.7). The node carries a collection-valued field and a closure sentinel, so one fixture exercises both motivating cases: deriving an indexed path (Columns[0].Label) needs the collection's current length, which no other read reports; and a value the wire format cannot carry is served as its sentinel string verbatim rather than refused, because an encoding WITH sentinels is the canonical encoding (rule 2). That same rule is why the payload is for reading and path derivation, never for round-tripping back as a node copy.

Whole-subtree fidelity (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.7 rule 3): a parent's encoding carries its descendants, with no depth limit and no elided variant. The rule needs its own fixture because an elided encoding is WELL-FORMED wire JSON for a different node, so a runner checking only well-formedness would pass exactly what the rule forbids. A runner should assert that every child the peer itself reports for this node appears inside the encoding it returned; the node kinds and child sets differ legitimately between hosts, so that is the host-agnostic form of the check.
Capability-gated mutation accepted: a canonical TreeOp embedded as a JSON object, advisory attribution, and the post-op tree revision (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.2).
Change subscription established; the response carries a baseline tree revision so the client has a known starting point (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.5).
Subscription released. Releasing an unknown or already-released subscriptionId also returns ok — the caller desired end state is reached either way (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.5).
Change event caused by a relay apply; id is the subscribe request id, treeRevision is the state after the change (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.5).
Change event the host caused itself. A peer that cannot distinguish the cause must emit "host" (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.5).
MANDATED CLASS 1 of 3. The host has not opted into relay exposure; nothing about the request was examined. Applies to any request type including hello (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.4, 11.1).
MANDATED CLASS 2 of 3. The op decoded but is not a legal edit of this tree — the user should change the edit (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.3, 8.4).

MANDATED CLASS 3 of 3. The op was understood and legal, but the host policy layer refused it — nothing the edit can fix. detail is deliberately empty: a refusal explaining why policy refused hands out a map of the policy (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.4, 11.5).
The apply op is not decodable as a TreeOp. detail carries the wire format DecodeError envelope verbatim (WIRE_FORMAT 6).
A recognised request type whose capability was not advertised. Distinct from UNKNOWN_MESSAGE: the entry point exists, this host simply does not offer it (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 6.4, 10.1).
A type outside the closed set. A well-formed message from a verified peer always gets an answer — silence is reserved for messages failing the origin checks (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 10.1).
Profile negotiation returned Foreign — a different major is never tolerable, since it may have removed a shape this peer relies on (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 5.2).
Structurally invalid payload — subscribe with an empty events array (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 8.5, 9.3).

No node with the requested id. For read.renderedDom a node present in the tree but not currently rendered uses reason "not-rendered", so a client can tell "no such node" from "not on screen" (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.4).
The named slot is not a binding slot on that node kind. Distinct from the noOverride STATUS, which means the slot exists and holds nothing (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.3).

The node exists and the host cannot produce its canonical wire encoding (DEVTOOLS_RELAY 7.7, 9.3). Distinct from NODE_NOT_FOUND, which would be a lie about a node that is plainly there and would send the client to look somewhere else — the one remedy that cannot help. No shipped host can raise this from its own surface: sentinels make the canonical encoder total over live trees. So a runner answers this fixture from a host whose SURFACE is made to return the encode-failed outcome, which tests the peer's mapping from that outcome onto the class — the part a host with a wider local vocabulary than the wire's would depend on, and the technique refusal-decode-failed and refusal-validator-reject already use.
